title: The Jealousy of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The jealousy of God means that God rightly refuses to share His worship, covenant love, or glory with idols. His jealousy is holy zeal for His own name and for the faithfulness of His people.
summary: The jealousy of God means that God rightly refuses to share His worship, covenant love, or glory with idols. His jealousy is holy zeal for His own name and for the faithfulness of His people.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals God’s jealous love by redeeming a people for Himself. He will not share His bride with idols, false gods, or rival lords.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s jealousy is not sinful insecurity. Human jealousy is often selfish, fearful, or possessive in corrupt ways. God’s jealousy is holy because He alone is worthy of ultimate worship and covenant loyalty.

Scripture forbids idolatry because worship belongs to God alone. False gods, created things, power, pleasure, comfort, approval, and self-rule have no right to the place that belongs to the Lord.

God’s jealousy is also covenantal. He loves His people and refuses to treat spiritual adultery as harmless. Idolatry destroys worship, distorts identity, and leads people away from life.

In Christ, God redeems people for Himself. Believers are not saved to keep serving rival masters. They are called into faithful devotion to the Lord who bought them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people think idolatry is only bowing before statues. Scripture shows that idols can be anything trusted, loved, feared, or obeyed above God. God’s jealousy exposes the heart’s divided worship.

This doctrine protects love from becoming compromise. God’s refusal to share His people with idols is not cruelty; it is holy faithfulness. He calls them away from death and back to Himself.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Examine what competes with God for your trust, love, fear, obedience, and identity. Repent of idols, visible and hidden. Worship the Lord alone, and let Christ reclaim every part of your life from rival masters.
